dream: The rough scrap bit into a flat stone until the gap yawned open. The tall tree leaned against it, drunk on weight, while the turnip sat heavy on the stack, feeling real enough to matter. The card hummed warm at fifty-four, making the heavy top edge feel like a drawing of pressure. I pressed down until the slip refused to move, proving the lean worked. Then the air grew thin and the tall tree slid away, leaving only the memory of a corner that felt sharp.
